name: Airwallex
summary: Multi-currency business accounts, corporate cards, international transfers and payment acceptance.
best_for: companies invoicing or paying in several currencies, where a 0.5% spread against your bank's 2–3% is the whole business case
skip_if: you bill in one currency and pay domestic suppliers — the multi-currency machinery is the product, and without FX volume you are paying a platform fee for a bank account
honest_knock: The honest headline here is that the FX markup is published at all — 0.5% and 1% above interbank is a real number, and most competitors will not print one. What the page does not settle is everything around it. The Grow plan's platform fee 'varies with team size' with no table, so the $12 a user is not the whole subscription -- though their table does say the first ten Spend users are free, which is the part the headline rate hides in your favour. Chargeback and dispute fees are not priced anywhere, only mentioned as a feature. And the page's own disclaimer says per-transaction fees apply to certain transactions with the detail in a separate fee schedule. So: use the published FX rate to compare against your bank, then ask for the fee schedule and the platform fee before you move money.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month per active Spend user plus a team-size platform fee

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (2026-08-28, read off their own pricing page and fee table; no rate below has changed since 1 Aug 2026) FX conversion 0.5% above the interbank rate for major currencies and 1% for all others. Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. Payment acceptance 2.8% + $0.30 on domestic cards and 4.30% + $0.30 on international cards; local payment methods $0.30 plus method-specific fees. Corporate cards carry no international fees and up to 2% cash rebate on local USD spend. Account plans: Explore free, Grow $12 per active Spend user/month plus a platform fee that varies with team size, Accelerate custom. Their table adds limits the earlier reading did not record: the first 10 Spend users are free and the $12 rate runs to 250 Spend users; the monthly fee is charged per business legal entity, with up to 3 entities included and $1,000 per additional entity; subscription and usage-based billing cost 0.50% per successful transaction while invoicing is free; and USD balances earn a Yield rate that Airwallex restamps daily rather than fixing per plan — on 5 September 2026 the page showed 3.22% on Explore, 3.37% on Grow and 3.49% on Accelerate, and its own footnote reads that the indicative rate is the 7-day annualised historical rate of the underlying funds as of 4 September 2026, net of fees. Read those three figures as a moving number carrying the date the page gave it, not as a plan feature: they were 3.21%, 3.36% and 3.48% when we first recorded them on 28 August 2026. (yield re-verified 5 Sep 2026) Platform API and embedded finance are quote-only. Two gaps we had left open got a partial answer on 17 September 2026, when Airwallex pointed us at its fee schedule. Dispute handling does carry a price, but only the Canadian entity publishes it: airwallex.com/en-ca/terms/fee-schedule prints 15 CAD per chargeback request and 0.30 CAD per refund request, both excluding whatever the card network passes on. The US pricing page lists dispute management as a feature with no fee beside it, so treat the Canadian figures as the shape of the charge rather than as your rate. The Grow platform fee is still not a number anywhere: both the US pricing page and the Canadian schedule say only that it is based on the total number of Spend users, so ask for it before you budget. Re-verified 2026-09-19 on airwallex.com/en-us/pricing: every published rate above is unchanged — FX, transfers, acquiring, the 0.50% on subscription billing, the free first 10 Spend users, the 250-user ceiling on the $12 rate and the $1,000 per entity beyond three. The yield figures still read 3.22%, 3.37% and 3.49%, but their footnote now dates the seven-day annualised rate to 18 September 2026 instead of 4 September. That is the clearest evidence yet that these three numbers are a daily restamp rather than a plan feature: same values, new date. The Grow platform fee is still not printed anywhere.
